premises: Solute atoms (Fe, Ni, Cr, Mn) can locally cluster in the stressed lattice under intermediate deformation conditions.
Transient short-range ordered clusters form dynamically near dislocation cores and act as temporary obstacles.
This clustering increases yield strength by pinning dislocations while still allowing dislocation glide to maintain ductility.
At lower strain rates, ordering is too weak due to slow kinetics; at higher strain rates, there is insufficient time for clustering.
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution after casting and solution heat treatment.
